hypothesis: Late-game knocks are inherently riskier as the opponent has had more turns to improve their hand. Raising the risk floor as the stock depletes will prevent overconfident late-game knocks that lead to undercuts.
rationale: The current confidence floor only scales with deadwood. Adding a stock-depletion term (max(0, 21 - stock_size)) protects against late-game undercuts where the opponent's hand is probabilistically stronger regardless of trace events.
